fixes.explanation: Whoa, hold on, friend. I think the word "distress" made you brace for a sad ending. The writer says, “In my distress I called to the LORD, and He answered and set me free.” (Psalm 118:5). He called, the LORD answered, and he was set free. I've been stuck in a tight spot myself, so I know that's the ending you want.

Ooh, so close, friend! Look at what the writer says: “The LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation.” (Psalm 118:14). Salvation is sitting right there in the line, and the LORD is the One who became it. Strength, a song AND salvation, all in one verse! I'd have been happy with just the song.

Not quite, friend, but you're in good company, because this one is easy to rush past. The writer says, “This is from the LORD, and it is marvelous in our eyes.” (Psalm 118:23). So the LORD is the One behind the rejected stone becoming the cornerstone. And the writer calls it marvelous! I think that's a good reason to stop for a second and just marvel.
